name: Corebridge Financial, Inc.

profile.description: Corebridge Financial, formerly AIG's Life & Retirement business (IPO September 2022), is a Houston-based provider of retirement and insurance products in four segments. Individual Retirement sells fixed, fixed-indexed and variable annuities. Group Retirement provides defined contribution recordkeeping and advice. Life Insurance writes U.S. term and universal life policies and also operates in the UK and Ireland. Institutional Markets offers pension risk transfer, stable value wraps and GICs. Marc Costantini, formerly of Manulife, became CEO on December 1, 2025. Corebridge has agreed to an all-stock merger with Equitable Holdings into a new holding company (Mountain Holding / 'New Equitable'), under which each Corebridge share converts into 1.000 New Equitable share; definitive proxy materials were filed in 2026. Market cap is about $15.7B.

innovation.label: WEAK
innovation.analysis: Track Record (1/3): Corebridge's main strategic moves have been structural rather than product-led: separating from AIG through the 2022 IPO and now agreeing to an all-stock combination with Equitable Holdings [5][6]. No new product category or revenue stream launched in the last five years was found. AI Deployment (0/2): The only AI-related finding is 10-K risk language citing 'the use of artificial intelligence' as a technological challenge to the business. No AI products or quantified AI savings were found [4]. Market Share (1/2): Corebridge is a meaningful player across annuities, group retirement and pension risk transfer, with about $416B of total assets, but no data showing category leadership or share gains was found [2]. Pipeline (0/2): No next-generation products with timelines were disclosed. Management attention is on the Equitable merger [6]. R&D Intensity (0/1): No R&D spending is reported [2].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Corebridge's purpose of helping people plan, save for and achieve secure retirements is clear and socially useful, but it does not stand out from annuity and retirement peers. Its pending absorption into New Equitable also clouds whether it will last as an independent identity [6]. Community Impact (1/2): Filings describe employee volunteering and a partnership with the Foundation for Financial Planning to expand pro bono financial planning for at-risk Americans. That is meaningful, but no dollar commitments were found [7]. Employee Retention (0/2): Leadership turnover is high. The CEO changed in December 2025, CFO Elias Habayeb resigned and was replaced by interim CFO Christopher Filiaggi, and the merger will move finance leadership to Equitable's Robin Raju [4]. Insider Buying (0/2): No meaningful net insider buying was found.

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on the Growth sleeve formula. The 2.8% yield ($0.99 TTM on $35.29) exceeds 2%, but dividends date only to the 2022 IPO, short of the 5-year history the Dividend sleeve requires [2][8]. D/E of 102% ($10.87B of debt against $10.65B of common equity) scores 0.86 [2]. TTM ROE of 8.3% (about $889M of net income to common) scores 0.56 at 2x weight, and the TTM net margin of 9.6% scores 0.48 [2]. Revenue growth of -2.8% YoY in Q2 2026 (third-party aggregator figure) scores 0.57 [3]. Forward P/E of 6.2 (FY2027 consensus EPS $5.73) scores 1.0, and forward PEG of 0.24 (6.2x divided by 25% expected EPS growth from FY2026 to FY2027) scores 1.0 at 2x weight [9]. The 5-year revenue CAGR is excluded: FMP's reported revenue series switches definitions between FY2021 and FY2022 (from $22.1B to $1.9B), so it cannot be compared [2]. Weighted sum is 6.02 of 8, which rounds to 8. Liquidity is about $165M a day.

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (6/9): Corebridge's economics depend on spread income from a roughly $265B investment portfolio, regulated statutory capital and long-duration annuity and pension liabilities [2]. These are balance-sheet businesses that AI cannot replicate, and state insurance regulation adds a moat. Exposure is greater in Group Retirement recordkeeping and advice and in retail distribution, where AI-driven advice and administration automation could compress fees and advisor-mediated sales. The company's own 10-K flags AI as a source of 'new and intensified challenges' [4]. AI Opportunity (0/1): No AI-related revenue is disclosed [4].

infinite_game.summary: Through Sinek's lens, Corebridge has been shaped mainly by its owners' finite goals. AIG carved it out for monetization, management has prioritized buybacks ($300M in Q2 2026 alone), the CEO and CFO have both changed within a year, and the company has now agreed to fold its identity into New Equitable. Retirement security is a worthy cause, but Corebridge as an institution has not shown it is built to keep playing on its own.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): Helping Americans reach financial security in retirement is service-oriented and could be a Just Cause, but Corebridge has not developed it into a distinctive, lived identity. Its strategy since the IPO has centered on capital return and now on combining with Equitable [5][6].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): Leadership has been unstable. Kevin Hogan stepped down and outsider Marc Costantini took over in December 2025, the CFO resigned and was replaced by an interim CFO, and the pending merger names Equitable executives to key roles [4]. A Built In culture summary, which it notes is AI-generated, describes experiences varying by business line, with workload and responsiveness complaints [4].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): Management communications focus on run-rate EPS, core sources of income and capital return targets [3]. No acknowledgment of rivals' strengths as a basis for self-improvement was found. The decision to combine with Equitable is about scale rather than learning.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Corebridge has changed form significantly, from AIG division to standalone public company in 2022 and now to a planned combination with Equitable Holdings under a new holding company [5][6]. These are ownership and structural changes rather than a reinvention of what the business does, so they earn only partial credit.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (0/2): Capital allocation favors shareholder distributions: $412M returned in Q2 2026 (including $300M of buybacks) with about $350M more planned for the second half, while operating EPS fell to $1.12 from $1.22 [3]. Weighted shares have fallen from about 646M in FY2022 to 454M [2]. No costly long-term capability bet was found.

investment_thesis: Corebridge trades at 6.2x FY2027 consensus EPS of $5.73 and about 1.5x book, with a 2.8% dividend yield. Consensus expects EPS to grow from $4.57 in FY2026 to $7.60 by FY2029 [2][9]. Underlying earnings are healthier than headline results suggest: excluding variable investment income, Q2 2026 operating EPS rose 14% YoY, and run-rate operating EPS of $1.35 was up 16% [3]. Buybacks are aggressive, with weighted shares down from 646M in FY2022 to 454M [2]. The pending all-stock merger with Equitable (1.000 New Equitable share per Corebridge share) would create a retirement company with more than $30B of pro forma GAAP book value and more than $25B of statutory capital, giving Corebridge holders scale and diversification [6].
thesis_continued: The bear case starts with earnings quality and volatility. GAAP results swing widely on derivative and market-risk-benefit marks: a $664M loss in Q1 2025, $814M of profit in Q4 2025 and a $16M loss to common in Q2 2026 [2]. Q2 2026 operating EPS fell to $1.12 from $1.22 and adjusted pre-tax operating income fell to $664M from $842M on weaker variable investment income [3]. Leverage of about 102% debt-to-equity and roughly 39x assets-to-equity leaves the company sensitive to credit losses in a $265B investment portfolio [2]. The Equitable merger brings integration risk, leadership changes and loss of Corebridge's independent identity. With a fixed exchange ratio, CRBG's price will increasingly trade with Equitable's stock rather than on Corebridge's own fundamentals [6].
key_catalysts: Shareholder votes and regulatory approvals for the all-stock combination with Equitable Holdings (1.000 New Equitable share per CRBG share), which would form a retirement company with more than $30B of pro forma book value [6]
Q3 2026 earnings in early November 2026, testing whether core sources of income can keep growing as variable investment income stays weak [3]
Continued capital return, with about $350M more targeted for the second half of 2026 after $412M returned in Q2 [3]
key_risks: Merger execution and identity risk: integration with Equitable, executive turnover (new CEO in December 2025, interim CFO) and a fixed exchange ratio that ties CRBG's value to Equitable's stock [4][6]

Credit and spread risk in a roughly $265B investment portfolio with about 39x financial leverage; private-credit or commercial real estate losses would directly hit statutory capital and buyback capacity [2]
Weaker variable investment income and lower rates compressing spreads; adjusted pre-tax operating income fell from $842M to $664M YoY in Q2 2026 [3]
